A forensic examination of Canada's federal lobbying registry. Every communication logged. Every policy outcome correlated. Every dollar traced through public records that your government hoped you'd never read.

The Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying maintains a public registry at lobbycanada.gc.ca documenting every registered interaction between lobbyists and federal officials. The OCL Annual Reports record that over 359,000 communications have been logged since modern reporting began. This investigation cross-references those records with Elections Canada financial returns, Parliamentary Budget…

Canada's federal lobbying system is vast, legal, and meticulously documented. The Office of the Commissioner of Lobbying (OCL) requires every individual paid to communicate with federal officials on behalf of a client or employer to register and report their activities. The result is one of the most detailed influence databases in any democracy — and almost nobody reads it.
